items.kind: semantics (S–M) — analyzer, method resolution vs std
items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-08 (incr-48's find, Order 48; met building M121's reach record)
items.title: a user's exported blanket impl in a MODULE makes std's OWN method calls ambiguous: `export impl type T with Describe { fun describe(self): str }` in `describe.vl` turns std's `items.describe(serializer)` (`std/src/wire.vl:601`, `:608`) into "'describe' is ambiguous on 'List<T>': both 'Wire' and 'Describe' provide it" — the same blanket written in the ENTRY is invisible to std
items.discussion: incr-48 (Order 48); B515 (a trait's methods resolve only in a file that imports the trait); B553 (the entry's impls and the pre-entry resolve); M121
items.body: Repro (vilan 0.45.0 @e75bc57c, `vilan run main.vl` in a package; files under `sweeps/order48/incr-48/finds/user-blanket-std-ambiguity/`): `describe.vl`: `export trait Describe { fun describe(self): str; }` / `export impl type T with Describe { fun describe(self): str { "mine" } }`; `main.vl`: `import std::io::print; import pkg::describe::Describe; fun main() { print(Describe::describe(4)); }` -> two errors located in std's `wire.vl` (601, 608), 'describe' is ambiguous on `List<T>` and on `usize`. Written in the entry (`inference::traits::b511_a_qualified_call_reaches_a_blanket_through_a_bound_and_a_tuple_subject` does exactly that) it compiles, because std resolves before the entry walks. Cause: std's own member lookups consult every impl the world holds, and B515's trait-scope rule (a trait's methods resolve only where the trait is imported) is not applied to std's files (std is exempt from importing what it calls) — so a package trait std has never heard of competes with std's `Wire::describe` at std's call sites. Expected: std's calls resolve among the traits STD's files reach; a package blanket cannot make std's code ambiguous. M121's reach record does not count std's own questions against an ENTRY impl for exactly this reason (otherwise B553's deferred order would surface this error for that b511 pin). Sizing S–M (solver).

items.title: a module's `Context::new()` whose only `run` is in the ENTRY still reports "`+` on `T` needs `T: Add` … `T` is unbounded" when the whole world resolves after the entry walks — B553's context half is not an order question: the same `run` in any module (loaded before or after the context's) grounds `T`
items.discussion: incr-48 (Order 48); B553 (the second shape); spec/contexts.md §8.1 (a context takes its type from its first run)
items.body: Repro (files under `sweeps/order48/incr-48/finds/entry-run-context/`): `c.vl`: `import std::context::Context; export let flavor = Context::new(); export fun read_it(): i32 { flavor.get() + 1 }`; `main.vl`: `import pkg::c::{ flavor, read_it }; fun main() { flavor.run(5, || { print(read_it()); }); }` -> the error at c.vl:3. Move the `run` into `a.vl` (loads BEFORE `c.vl`) or `r.vl` (after) and call it from main: clean, prints 6. incr-48 built B553's impl half as a deferred order (the world resolves once, after the entry walks) and tried it here: the deferred order reports the same error, so the entry's `run` does not ground a module's context in a single resolve either — something about the ENTRY's use (the entry walks in the global scope with `entry_phase` set; a module's does not) keeps the run from filling the context's value slot. Pinned ignored: `inference::modules::b553_a_module_context_grounded_only_by_an_entry_run` (`B553:` reason). Sizing S–M (solver: the context value slot's grounding).
